bottleneck:
Long-form views, and with them watch hours. Lifetime that's about 1,013 views ≈ 68 h against 4,000, and one video (EloraTZP, 523) is 52% of it. Four things cost the most this week:
(1) Long-form topics went to low-demand lanes: cost/Medicare got 3, a gray-market pharmacy check got 6 and food got 11. The only lane with a signal is fresh named next-gen news (median 47, n=5, against 8 for approved-drug deep dives), and it got 1 long-form in 6 days (petrelintide 10-25).
(2) Next-gen news, our strongest topic family (retatrutide Shorts reached 257 and 197), was routed into Shorts, and both of those Shorts were dropped for music masking (10-24 S1 at 0.038, 10-25 S1 at 0.037). 5 of 18 Shorts this week were lost to masking alone.
(3) No working funnel. No Short has ever carried a working link to a live long-form. 10-25 L1 shipped a watch-next link to a video that doesn't exist (404), and description line 1 has missed the link 7 times.
(4) We steer blind. Retention, CTR, traffic sources, subscribers and real watch time are all missing, and 10-21 to 10-25 is only partly logged.
playbook_markdown:
# InforMed growth playbook: week of 2026-10-26

**Status:** off track. About 68 of 4,000 watch hours. This week's long-form median is 8.5 views (n=4) against the 30+ target. Long-form watch time is the only way into YPP: every slot below is ranked by how much it moves that.

## Long-form (1 a day, 14:00 ET, 8–12 min): pick in this order every day
1. **Lane C, fresh named news (Exp C).** Use it when a named next-gen drug (retatrutide, CagriSema, survodutide, petrelintide, amycretin, MariTide, orforglipron's new indications) has a trial result or regulatory step that **first became public within 48 h**.
   - A journal paper of an old topline counts only if it adds new data. Check the first-report date before you claim "new".
   - New drug name first in the title. Label it `lane: C`.
   - **News beats Shorts:** if the radar finds qualifying news, it goes to the long-form first. A Short on it is the 20:00 funnel Short.
2. **Pipeline decoder "What Is [drug]?"** (1–2 this week, no-news days only). For an under-covered drug with published human data: amycretin, MariTide, pemvidutide, mazdutide.
   - Generic name first, a dated status in the first 30 s, no "beat" frame. Label it `lane: P`.
3. **Lane A, practical tirzepatide (Exp A).** Use it on the remaining days. The Strength Training model only. Examples:
   - "Protein on Tirzepatide: How Much and Why"
   - "What Happens When You Stop Tirzepatide?" (trial evidence, plus "don't stop or change your medicine on your own")
   - "Tirzepatide and Hair Loss: How Common and What Helps"
   - Label it `lane: A`. Don't repeat 10-24 Side Effects or 10-21 What to Eat.
- **Banned in long-form:**
  - Cost, coverage and Medicare topics.
  - Gray-market and pharmacy topics (Lane B is closed).
  - Single-trial deep dives on approved drugs.
  - Timeline-only questions.
  - "Did X beat Y?" without a randomized head-to-head trial.
  - Repeating a Short topic from the last 14 days (unless it's the Lane C news itself).

## Long-form packaging and retention
- **Title:** about 60 characters or fewer, drug name first, the searched phrase or the new name up front. At most 1 number. Spell out abbreviations. It must be fully paid off in the video.
- **Thumbnail:** 4 words or fewer, never a repeat of the title. One labelled drug or character, one honest emotion.
- **0–15 s:** what the viewer will know by the end, plus the first concrete answer.
  - Re-hook every 45–75 s.
  - Name chapters after the questions people search for.
  - One subscribe ask, after the payoff.
- **Ending:** name one live long-form in the same series by its exact YouTube title: EloraTZP or Orforglipron for lanes C/P, Strength Training for lane A. Then the end screen.

## Shorts (3 a day, at most 170 words, 60–85 s)
- **13:00, lead:** pick one:
  - a two-drug head-to-head with tirzepatide named first and a different trial each time;
  - a tirzepatide muscle outcome question ("How much of the weight lost is muscle?");
  - a gray-market "what's confirmed?" question with a new dated FDA/MHRA/manufacturer fact (at most 1 a week).
- **08:00:** a calm "honest uncertainty" body-worry Short (bone, gallbladder, pancreas, hair). Tirzepatide in the title where the evidence covers it. This is the Instagram winner.
- **20:00, funnel Short (Exp D):** a spin-off of a live long-form. Rotate in this order:
  1. that day's Lane C long-form, if one is live;
  2. EloraTZP;
  3. Strength Training on Tirzepatide.
  - Ask a fresh single question the long-form answers; never re-cut the long-form's own script.
  - Last spoken line: "Full breakdown: [exact live title], on our channel."
  - Put the URL in description line 1 and the pinned comment, **after confirming it opens that exact video (oEmbed)**. If you can't verify it, say "follow for more" and don't count the Short toward Exp D.
- **Banned:**
  - "Is X approved yet?" titles.
  - "3 Ways…" lists.
  - Brand-first or semaglutide-only titles (unless that's the evidence).
  - Cost or coverage Shorts.
  - Observational surgery angles.
  - Titles that name no drug.
  - Scare framing.
- **Variety guard:** any one trial in at most 1 Short a week, no back-to-back same-template titles, a new fact in every piece.

## Quality gates (non-negotiable)
- **Mix Shorts at masking 0.02 or lower first time** (copy the long-form music level). Measure last. Above 0.03 is an automatic drop: 5 Shorts were lost this week.
- Captions come from the on-screen text: numbers match their stat pills exactly, and no split numbers or trial names.
- Every piece carries "Not personal advice" and "talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you". No dosing, no switching or stopping advice, no compounded or online sources. The fact-checker and the Editor-in-Chief always win.

## Carousels (until the owner decides)
- Reuse verified Short text only. No new research. Spend the time on caption, number and link checks.

## Experiments (apply exactly; log `lane` in every long-form's metadata)
- **Exp A:** lane A only on no-news, no-decoder days. Practical tirzepatide topics. Score at day 7 and day 28.
- **Exp C:** every qualifying news day. Score at day 7 against the GLP-1 long-form median of 20.
- **Exp D:** every 20:00 Short is a verified-link funnel Short. The analyst records the target long-form's views for the 3 days before and after each one.
- **Lane P** is tracked, not yet an experiment. Report it separately from C.
- **Hold constant:** 14:00 ET, 8–12 min, the same retention rules.

experiments.name: Exp A: Search-question long-forms (practical tirzepatide)
experiments.hypothesis: Long-forms on practical 'get the most from tirzepatide' questions people search (strength training, protein, side effects, stopping) will beat approved-drug deep dives (median 8) and keep gaining views over time. Strength Training (48, still climbing at day 9) is the model.
experiments.change: Lane A runs on no-news, no-decoder days (2–3 this week): practical tirzepatide topics only, searched phrase first, about 60 characters or fewer, at most 1 number. Cost, coverage and timeline-only topics are excluded from now on. Slot, length and retention rules stay the same.
experiments.metric: Views at day 7 and day 28. Success: day-7 median of 25 or more and still growing at day 28. Once the API is on, also average view duration and watch hours per video.
experiments.min_sample: n=8 videos to call it (about 11-03 to 11-05). Judge each video at day 7 and day 28.
experiments.result: Interim, below target. In-window logged: How Long 26, What to Eat 11 (day 4), Medicare 3 (day 2): median 11, n=3. Side Effects (10-24) isn't logged yet. Including Strength Training from before the experiment (48): median 18.5, n=4. Cost topics are removed from the lane after Medicare got 3 (anecdote).

experiments.name: Exp B: Gray-market 'what's actually confirmed' long-forms
experiments.hypothesis: Our strongest Short lane (gray-market 'what's confirmed?', median about 105, n=7) would also work as long-form.
experiments.change: 2 long-forms a week in lane B, credited and dated, no sellers named.
experiments.metric: Day-7 views compared with the GLP-1 long-form median. Success: day-7 median of 33 or more.
experiments.result: Closed early at n=1. 'Semaglutide or Tirzepatide Online: How to Check a Pharmacy' got 6 views by day 3. That's an anecdote and doesn't prove the lane fails. We're stopping because each slot costs a probable Lane A or C video (medians 18.5 and 47), and the lane sits close to 'online sources' policy risk. Gray-market stays a Shorts-only lane (at most 1 a week). Any retest has to go through Lane C with a fresh dated FDA, MHRA or manufacturer event.

experiments.name: Exp C: First explainer within 48 h of a newly named drug or result
experiments.hypothesis: Being the first clear explainer of a new named result with little search competition (EloraTZP 523) drives long-form views far more than any title formula.
experiments.change: When a named next-gen drug's result or regulatory step first becomes public within 48 h, that day's long-form explains it with the drug name first in the title. Qualifying news goes to the long-form before any Short. A journal publication of an old topline counts only if it adds new data.
experiments.metric: Day-7 views compared with the GLP-1 long-form median (20, n=17) and approved-drug deep dives (8). Success: day-7 median of 50 or more.
experiments.min_sample: n=4 qualifying videos made after 10-20 (probably 2–4 weeks, depending on news).
experiments.result: In-window n=1: petrelintide (10-25), not logged yet; score it at day 7 on 11-01. Looking back at earlier fresh-news next-gen long-forms: median 47 (n=5: 523, 56, 47, 25, 18), a signal. Missed this week: two next-gen news topics (retatrutide sleep apnea, retatrutide kidneys) went to Shorts and were both dropped for masking. Note: TRIUMPH-1 OSA results were first announced on 6 Jun 2026, so the radar must check the first-report date before calling anything 'new'.

experiments.name: Exp D: Shorts-to-long-form funnel with a verified link
experiments.hypothesis: A funnel Short that asks a fresh question its live long-form answers will lift that long-form's daily views when it ends by naming the exact title and carries a working, verified link. Shorts average about 60 YouTube views each and currently send no measurable traffic to long-form.
experiments.change: Every 20:00 Short is a spin-off of a live long-form, rotating between that day's Lane C video, EloraTZP and Strength Training on Tirzepatide. Last spoken line: 'Full breakdown: [exact live title], on our channel.' The oEmbed-verified URL goes in description line 1 and the pinned comment. Only the presence of the working link and CTA changes; topic rules stay the same.
experiments.metric: The target long-form's views in the 3 days after the Short against the 3 days before (from daily snapshots). Once the API is on, use 'Shorts feed' and 'related video' traffic sources. Success: average lift of 10 or more views a day, or 50% or more over the baseline.
experiments.min_sample: n=6 funnel Shorts with a verified working link. Shorts that ship without a verified link are excluded.
experiments.result: Started 2026-10-26. Baseline: no Short has ever shipped with a working long-form link. EloraTZP and Strength Training are each gaining roughly 1–3 views a day.

owner_decisions: Enable the YouTube Analytics API (Google Cloud → APIs & Services → YouTube Analytics API → Enable) and send monetization_progress. Why: partner_progress is still null. Our 68 watch hours are a guess at 4 minutes a view; the real figure could be 40 or 100 hours. Without it we can't see retention, CTR, traffic sources or subscribers, so Exp D can only be judged from rough view deltas. Expected effect: real YPP tracking, the ability to retitle long videos with low CTR after 48 h, and a clean read on the funnel.

Lower the default music and sound-effect level in the Shorts template to the long-form level, and make the renderer re-mix automatically until masking is 0.02 or lower. Why: 5 of 18 Shorts this week were dropped for masking at 0.034–0.039, including both retatrutide Shorts. Retatrutide is our highest-peak topic (257, 197). All 15 long-forms mixed at 0.002–0.018. Expected effect: about 5 more Shorts shipped a week, which at the 62 median is about 300 more YouTube Shorts views a week, plus more subscriber and funnel chances.

Make link verification block publishing. Before anything publishes, check every watch-next URL in descriptions and pinned comments with oEmbed. Also log every post with its lane label. Why: 10-25 L1 shipped a watch-next link to a video that doesn't exist (404), line 1 has missed the link 7 times, and posts from 10-21 to 10-25 are only partly logged. Expected effect: Exp D can run at all, and next week's review can score Exp A and C instead of guessing.

In Studio: (a) add EloraTZP or Strength Training on Tirzepatide as the related video on our 5 best-performing GLP-1 Shorts and on every new funnel Short; (b) create the playlists 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded' (EloraTZP, Orforglipron, Survodutide, Retatrutide, CagriSema, Petrelintide) and 'Life on GLP-1' (Strength Training, How Long, What to Eat, Side Effects), and set them as end-screen elements. Why: EloraTZP is 523 of our 1,013 lifetime long-form views and still growing, and the related-video link is Studio-only. Expected effect: the first real Shorts-to-long traffic. Even 5–10 more long views a day would be a 7–14% lift on our current ~70 a day.

Stop the daily 17:30 carousel (a cadence change). Why: about 30 carousels have reached 0–3 each (proven). They cost a production slot and Claude usage every day while 7 Shorts were dropped this week. Expected effect: the freed effort goes into mix, caption and link checks now. If Exp C confirms the novelty effect (n=4), use it for a second long-form only on days with two qualifying Lane C news items.
